title: Ahorita
desc: One word, four meanings, and a whole afternoon
setting: Marcos said he would come by ahorita. That was two hours ago.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.en: Hello? Ideay, I am on my way out now.

options.en: Right. About how long will you be?
options.feedback: You accepted and asked for a number. That is the only way ahorita ever becomes a time.

options.en: All right, I will wait here.
options.feedback: Patient and pleasant. You have also agreed to wait an unknown amount of time.

options.en: You said ahorita two hours ago.
options.feedback: True, and it lands as a complaint about something nobody here counts as broken.

options.es: ¿Veinte minutos tuyos o veinte de verdad?
options.en: Twenty of your minutes or twenty real ones?
options.feedback: The joke Nicaraguans make about their own word. Making it yourself is the move.

options.en: All right, I will wait for you.
options.feedback: Fine. You have missed the joke that was sitting right there.

options.en: So you will arrive at five.
options.feedback: Sharp rather than funny. It reads as a telling-off.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Jaja, vos ya aprendiste. Veinte de verdad.
steps.en: Ha, you have learned. Twenty real ones.

options.en: I am getting the hang of it.
options.feedback: Light, self-deprecating, and it accepts the compliment without making a thing of it.

options.en: Yes, I know how it is.
options.feedback: True. A shade smug where the other one was warm.

options.es: Es que ustedes nunca llegan a la hora.
options.en: The thing is you people never arrive on time.
options.feedback: Ustedes turns a joke between two friends into a verdict on a country.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.en: See you in a bit, then.

options.feedback: You gave him his own word back. That is exactly how the call should end.
Correct and normal. It just leaves his joke unanswered.
The please turns it into a request, and now it is a small argument.
